Wendell Jackson

Independent candidate for Governor, Tennessee · Open seat

Spoken word performer and comedian (per Politics1 and Elections Simplified; his campaign site does not list an occupation)

Wendell Jackson is an independent candidate for Governor of Tennessee from Clarksville. He filed his nominating petition with the Tennessee Secretary of State on February 4, 2026, and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot. He describes his effort as a nonpartisan campaign that does not raise money.

Where Jackson stands

Economic development / Jobs
Says he wants to create jobs and improve employment services and job training. Supports local businesses and what he calls responsible economic growth and stability.
Cost of living / Housing
Lists housing stability and housing for all Tennesseans among his top priorities.
Health care
Supports healthcare for all Tennessee residents.
Government ethics / Transparency
Proposes giving residents access to the inner workings of the governor's office and inviting them to the State Capitol to ask about issues. He calls the governor the public's employee.
Campaign finance
Calls his campaign a 'no money campaign' and says it is nonpartisan and focused on upholding the constitution. State filings show $0 raised.
Education
Says gaining knowledge will be 'made paramount and encouraged.' He refers broadly to a STEAM-rich, logic-based 'Curriculum of Common Knowledge' but gives no specific schools proposal.
